message.content:
`contenteditable` is **not** a strict boolean attribute – it accepts three string values: | Value | Meaning | |-------|---------| | `"true"` | The element is editable. | | `"false"` | The element is not editable. | | `"plaintext-only"` | The element is editable, but only plain text can be entered (no formatting). | So when you want the element to be editable but restrict it to plain‑text input, you should set the attribute exactly to the string `"plaintext-only"`: ```html
…
``` There is no separate “boolean string” for this case; the literal string `"plaintext-only"` is the valid value. If you were converting a value programmatically, you would simply return `"plaintext-only"` when the input key is `"contenteditable"` and the value is `"plaintext-only"`.
